conf.description: aws-vpcflow tgw-flow / parquet-s3: maps the already-typed Parquet columns to ECS - protocol/tcp-flags decode (wider flag set than the VPC feed), the four packets-lost-* drop counters, epoch-seconds timestamps. No action column exists on TGW records, so event.outcome is deliberately left unset. Scope limited to the 13 integer-typed columns this work order tables; every other selected column is STRING-typed identically to the text TGW feed and maps to ECS exactly as that feed does.

conf.comment: aws-vpcflow / tgw-flow / parquet-s3. Own route/identity from the VPC flow pipeline (the work order's own warning: 'a shared route would let TGW columns be read against the VPC schema'). tcp-flags and the four packets-lost-* columns are HYPHENATED source names (THE BIG ONE trap), read via __e[] bracket access, never path syntax, then dropped via glob in eval.remove. TGW's tcp-flags documents a wider bit set than VPC (PSH=8, URG=32 in addition to FIN/SYN/RST/ACK), decoded here accordingly. No ACCEPT/REJECT action column exists on this record type, so event.outcome is left unset rather than defaulted - matching the Elastic-side instruction not to default it. Driving event.action from a non-zero drop counter is named only in the Elastic recommendation, not the Cribl one, so it is NOT done here - documented scope split. Direct route, no guard hop.

functions.description: record dataset, format, own-route rationale, and the wider tcp-flags / no-action-column / event.action scope decisions

step 1: cast the five hyphenated-source integer columns into FLAT clean-named scratch fields (no dots) via bracket access - kept flat rather than nested aws.vpcflow.* names at this stage so step 2 can read them back safely (a flat bracket read of a dotted target created by eval.add would silently miss it, same landmine documented in the sibling flow/parquet-s3 pipeline)

add.name: 'aws.vpcflow.tcp_flags_array'
add.value: [(__e['_tcp_flags_num'] & 1) !== 0 ? 'fin' : undefined, (__e['_tcp_flags_num'] & 2) !== 0 ? 'syn' : undefined, (__e['_tcp_flags_num'] & 4) !== 0 ? 'rst' : undefined, (__e['_tcp_flags_num'] & 8) !== 0 ? 'psh' : undefined, (__e['_tcp_flags_num'] & 16) !== 0 ? 'ack' : undefined, (__e['_tcp_flags_num'] & 32) !== 0 ? 'urg' : undefined]

functions.description: step 2, from ORIGINAL vendor names (protocol/start/end/version) and the step-1 flat scratch fields, before the batched rename: bounded protocol resolution (same 4-protocol scope as the VPC pipeline), tcp-flags bit decompose over the WIDER TGW flag set (fin=1/syn=2/rst=4/psh=8/ack=16/urg=32, no arrow/filter per constraint 3), the four drop counters, and epoch-seconds-to-ms/duration/_time (never @timestamp, constraint 1)
batch-rename the five clean 1:1 typed columns to their ECS targets

tag event.dataset (no hyphen, constraint 5) and event.provider; drop the clean-named originals consumed above, the hyphenated tcp-flags/packets-lost-* originals via glob (literal hyphenated names are rejected by eval.remove), and every flat scratch field
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
